title: Five hard earned lessons about Evals — Ankur Goyal, Braintrust
talk_summary: Ankur Goyal of Braintrust argues evals must be engineered as living specs (custom scorers, reconciled datasets) rather than off-the-shelf benchmarks, and that agent token budgets are dominated by tool definitions/outputs, not system prompts. He also shows that optimizing the whole system (data + prompt + tools + scorers) beats prompt-only optimization, and that ambitious evals let you ship a feature within days of a new model release.

takeaways.technique: Tool I/O as prompt engineering (YAML over JSON, LLM-shaped tools)
takeaways.what_they_do: Design tool definitions and outputs for what the LLM wants to see, not as a thin wrapper over existing APIs; switch verbose JSON outputs to token-efficient YAML for analysis tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: shifting the output of a tool from JSON to YAML actually made a significant difference... it's just so much more token efficient
takeaways.numbers: Claims tools/tool-responses dominate the token budget of modern agent prompts (vast majority of tokens not from system prompt)

takeaways.technique: Custom scorers as PRD/spec, not off-the-shelf
takeaways.what_they_do: Write and constantly modify your own scoring functions that encode your product spec, instead of using generic LLM-as-judge or open-source scorers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every company that we work with that's sufficiently advanced is writing their own scoring functions um and modifying them uh constantly

takeaways.technique: Feedback-to-eval pipeline with human taste filter
takeaways.what_they_do: Turn real user complaints into eval datapoints, but keep a human in the loop to select which feedback is worth adding rather than auto-ingesting everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we don't automatically take user feedback and add it to data sets right now. We actually want a human who has some taste

takeaways.technique: Provider-agnostic proxy + ambitious evals to exploit new models fast
takeaways.what_they_do: Route all model calls through a proxy so swapping providers needs no code change, and maintain ambitious evals that reveal when a new/cheaper model crosses viability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't need to change any code to work across model providers
takeaways.numbers: Feature went from ~10% (unviable) to viable across model generations; shipped first version two weeks after Claude 4 Sonnet launch

takeaways.technique: Optimize the whole system, not just the prompt
takeaways.what_they_do: When improving an agent, jointly optimize dataset, task/prompt/tools, and scorers; they benchmarked prompt-only vs whole-system optimization.
takeaways.evidence_quote: giving it the prompt the data set and the scores and said please optimize this whole system... there's a very dramatic difference
takeaways.numbers: Whole-system optimization produced a 'very dramatic' improvement over prompt-only, moving results from unviable to viable

takeaways.technique: Eval competence milestones (24h model adoption, feedback path, offense)
takeaways.what_they_do: Define concrete signs evals are working: can adopt a new model in 24h, can turn a complaint into an eval, and use evals to predict viability before shipping.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if a new model comes out uh you should be prepared um uh via your evals to be able to launch an update to your product within 24 hours
takeaways.numbers: Notion incorporates new models within 24 hours of release
